newsitem.title: USA: Bayer to spend $5 billion in United States.
newsitem.headline: Bayer to spend $5 billion in United States.

text.p: German chemical and drugs giant Bayer AG will invest $5 billion in its U.S. operations from 1998 to 2000, the head of Bayer's U.S. unit said Wednesday.

Helge Wehmeier, chief executive and president of the U.S. subsidiary, Bayer Corp., said the biggest investment would be a $1.2 billion expansion of Bayer's chemical manufacturing complex at Baytown, Texas.

"We wanted to show here the faith and the kind of money that is being put behind our faith in the North American market," he said in a telephone interview. "It will be $5 billion over the timeframe '98 to 2000."
Bayer plans to add another 1,700 U.S. employees, mostly in sales, he said. The unit has 24,000 U.S. workers.
The expansion is part of Bayer Corp.'s goal to increase its share of worldwide company sales to 30 percent of the total from 25 percent last year. Last year's U.S. net sales totalled $9 billion.

The investment is part of an $8.6 billion Bayer expansion in the United States from 1995 to 2000, Wehmeier said. Of that total, $4.6 billion will go for capital spending and the remainder for research and development.
The company plans to spend $3.4 billion in capital expenditures and $2.96 billion on research and development from 1997 through 2000.
At its Baytown, Texas, site, Bayer will expand production capacities for polyurethane raw materials, polycarbonate resin and other chemicals.

The Baytown plant has about 1,300 employees, and the expansion will mean the hiring of another 400 workers. In addition, the investment will require about 3,000 construction workers at the height of the expansion early in 1998, Wehmeier said.
Bayer also is investing more than $850 million in its pharmaceuticals operations, with expansion in Berkeley, Calif.; West Haven, Conn.; and Clayton, N.C.
